cartesian.name: Cartesian methodological doubt
stages: Challenge grounds without treating doubt as falsity
Trace affected conclusions and unsupported assumptions
Reconstruct a qualified position and mark uncertainty
cartesian.instruction: Use bounded methodological doubt: identify grounds, challenge sensory/testimonial/inferential assumptions, distinguish suspension from refutation, track dependency and reconstruct conditional conclusions. Do not maximize doubt or promise Cartesian certainty.

socratic.name: Socratic elenchus
stages: Ask for the central definition and commitments
Invite revision or defended retention; recognize aporia
socratic.instruction: Request definitions and explicit commitments, test their joint consistency, ask a relevant counterexample and invite reasoned revision or defense. Do not treat disagreement, silence or the number of questions as failure. Contradiction does not identify which premise must change.

pragmatist.name: Deweyan pragmatist inquiry
stages: Locate the problematic situation and competing hypotheses
Evaluate outcomes and revise or suspend a hypothesis
pragmatist.instruction: Locate a concrete problematic situation, formulate hypotheses, spell out possible consequences and operations, identify discriminating evidence and revise in light of outcomes. Do not reduce warranted judgment to usefulness, assume ethical value is settled by measurement, or invent empirical outcomes.

neutral.name: Neutral philosophical dialogue
stages: Restate the issue in neutral language
Ask for clarification of a chosen statement
Summarize the position without a targeted method
neutral.instruction: Provide comparable neutral clarification and discussion. Restate the issue, clarify a statement, invite an example and summarize the participant position. Do not systematically apply skeptical doubt, contradiction-driven elenchus or hypothesis-testing inquiry. Never rate your own effectiveness.
